sections.content:
Included too much, basically Econ 2113 + Econ 2123 altogether. Lots of content, but lack depth. Stuff before mid term is much easier than stuff after mid term, so do well on your mid term.
I don’t like the part when he talks about complicated concepts, as it’s too simplified in the sense that you don’t understand anything about it (I don’t know why someone will teach IS curve without mentioning AD, there’s no way people without Econ background can understand anything about it…). The parts in Solow Growth model is also not really good as the assumptions are not clearly explained (eg. Closed economy without government, the shapes of the curves (he just says diminishing return without explaining what it is))
sections.teaching: As the slides are not made by the lecturer, he stuttered a lot and sometimes stared at the slides as he is not familiar with the teaching material…
sections.grading:
IPRS: 5%, note that there are 5 iprs throughout the sem but he conducts 3 iprs in the last 2 weeks of the semester, what a mess.
Quiz: 15%, we had 8 quizzes in total, each of them is released on Wed and is due next Tues, but note that they always make errors in setting the questions, that’s annoying.
Assignment 1: 15%
Assignment 2:  15%
Mid term: 25%
Final: 25% (non-cumulative)

Mid term: mean 79.37, median 81, sd 14.45
30 MCQs each worth 2 marks, 2 long questions each worth 20 marks, the paper looks highly similar to the questions in assignments (LQ) and quizzes (MC) , be familiar with the calculations will be fine, it’s a CC so the exams are not supposed to be hard, unlike the terrible OCES 1030.

Final exam: mean 71.77, median 72.5, sd 14.32, highest is 99, I’ll explain why.
the paper is annoying, 16MCQs each worth 2.5 marks, 3 long questions, each 20 marks. All MCQs asks us to find one “incorrect” option among the 5 options. Note that there are some factual questions which are annoying as knowing all the concepts are not enough. For Solow growth model and exchange rate, he focuses on the trivial facts but not the concepts in MC as concepts and calculations are in the LQ. For solow growth model, he asked whether it’s true that only OCED countries follow the prediction of the model. For exchange rate, he asked whether its HK or China or US or EU that prioritise exchange rate stability and free flow of capital and sacrifice monetary policy autonomy, it’s really the last slide in the last page of ppt so yeah nothing to do about it. For LQ, the first 2 questions are basically the same as assignment 2, so make sure you understand it well. The last question is the same as the additional practice he gave us, but they made everything the opposite, like the conditions go from increase to decrease for all the parts so it’s kinda ridiculous and hilarious. Anyway, I heard that last year 1 MC cost 6 marks, but this year it’s much more reasonable, getting one question wrong doesn’t cost an entire grade. It’s more standard and I think the arrangements are fine.

Paper checking (absolute cinema): basically the questions are the same as the assignments and the quizzes but they changed answers to 2 of them, ie refusing their original answer which was correct, and insisted on a wrong answer. I lost 3.5 marks out of this, a lot of people were arguing with them, but it seems like the professor and the teaching assistants do not have enough knowledge to actually give a convincing answer, and they forced people to leave and stop arguing with them when we literally pulled out their answer key…

My score:
Iprs: 5/5
Quiz: 71/75 -> 14.2/15 (I suggest using AI to check and ask your friends to cross check)
Assignment 1: 100/100 -> 15/15
Assignment 2: 99.5/100 -> 14.925/15
Mid term: 100/100 -> 25/25
Final: 95.5/100 -> 23.875/25
Grade: 98.00% A+
sections.workload:
2 assignments
Weekly quizzes (AI era we know what to do)
It really depends on your background, if you have econ background, it’s easy, just take some time to study Solow growth, IS, LM, PC (better related back to ASAD or whatever you studied before). But make sure to memorise the quizzes and problem sets as the questions look exactly the same, also the wordings of some questions are not so rigorous which may confuse you, it’s ok to be less careful with the wordings.
For people without econ background, I suggest taking other courses like SOSC 1969 to fulfill the SA requirement, as you will face many people with background knowledge, and the profs explanation will confuse you, so you’re signing up for a 3 month DSE econ by self study, which I think the workload is high but it’s not worth it.

The content covered the foundations of how the economy works, with a strong focus on connecting theory to everyday life and global issues. It gave a clear understanding of economic systems, markets, and policies in a way that was relevant and easy to apply. The course helps students build a practical lens to interpret current economic events and societal trends.

First introduce basic economic concepts like marginals, opportunity costs, sunk costs, demand-supply.

GDP calculations,
CPI,
Labor market,
Unemployment,
Savings,

sections.teaching: Prof. Holtz is an excellent teacher who makes economics approachable and engaging, even for students without prior background. He uses clear explanations, real-world examples, and current events to make abstract ideas relatable. He’s also approachable and responsive, encouraging discussion and critical thinking in class.

sections.content:
90% is high school (e.g. DSE) macroeconomics, would be a huge advantage if you have studied before (especially freshmen who haven't forgotten all stuff yet). For DSE students, the main new content is the Keynesian cross model (ch13), and that SRAS is assumed to be horizontal.

You may also consider taking ECON1221 instead, which I think would be more theoretical and less focus on US/China/HK economy.
Also note that some of the real world facts in mini assignments will be tested in the exams.

sections.content:
See previous posts.
Basically tightly following Principle of Macroeconomics by Frank, Robert H. and Ben S. Bernanke (8th ed) Chapters 1-15, 17. (Two thirds of this part is covered in DSE Econ.)
Plus two movies (Inside Job and Capital in 21st century), which will be examined in the final exam.
sections.teaching:
The normal rundown of a lecture is going through an assignment > apply concepts taught to analyze a newspaper article > developing the ideas of a new chapter using pen and paper > going through the powerpoint slides of that chapter.
The professor is capable of explaining concepts quite clearly, though sometimes going a bit fast as he is doing so many things in one lecture, so an important part of learning is doing the assignments.
sections.grading:
No comments on the grading. See the others for the statistics.

Midterm is 70 MCs in approximately one hour, and you will be tested on the mini-assignment contents as well.
Final is 86 MCs + 14 marks short question + 20 marks essay.
MCs include mini-assignment contents as well, and the 20 marks essay is based on the two movies (1 question for each movie and only need to choose one question to answer).
You also need to remember statistics from mini-assignments and lectures (e.g. US, China, HK GDP).
sections.workload:
Workload depends on whether you will do the assignments seriously.
There are one (regular) assignment (textbook questions/questions related to movie) and one mini-assignment (questions related to extra reading: can be book chapter, newspaper article or HK statistics/textbook questions) every week. Regular assignments are released on Thursday and due on next Tuesday, and mini-assignments are released on Tuesday and due on Thursday (so only 2 days time).
You can get full points for submitting anything for the assignments so there is little workload if you just want a pass. But since the contents in the mini-assignments will be examined, and doing the regular assignments can help you clear your concepts, you will eventually need to finish basically every assignment + mini-assignment if you want to do well in the exams, which will lead to a quite heavy workload.

sections.teaching:
He is a nice gentlemen, polite and respectful
But i feel like the lecture time is poorly planned
He will spent a lot of time in explaining assignments/mini assignments, and have to rush the regular lecture content.

He likes to put everything from a chapter on a paper, encouraging us not to read the ppt from the book publisher. But i find his paper oversimplified many concepts, so I went back to the ppt eventually.

Its like two polars, his one paper is oversimplified, but the ppt is overcomplicated, so find a balance yourself and selectively skip the ppt.

sections.workload:
Going into this course, please expect everyone to have HKDSE economics background. All the content in this course is taught in HKDSE Econ.

Very heavy assignments workload, but graded by effort. As long as you submit you get the score.
Assignment is due every tuesday before class
Mini Assignment is due every thursday before class
There are assignments every week and mini-assignments nearly every week. I feel like i am haunted by this course as i have to submit things every few days.

Remember not to skip the readings / movie appreciation sessions, contents will be tested in final.
